subject: Request: sticky-version safeguard & auto-swap runbook for OrthonoVA pilot
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria@orthonova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orthonova.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:03:21 -0700
Subject: Elevated latency on Pilot canary - request for auto-fallback/pinning

Hi Kimberly,

We observed a sustained latency increase on the OrthonoVA pilot's inference route during the 08:40-09:00 PDT window. P50 jumped from ~45ms to 320ms and a small but growing fraction of requests hit the 2s tail.

This is impacting a user-facing cohort. Can you confirm whether Redwood has an automated fallback or sticky-version/pin option we can enable immediately? Our SREs would prefer an automated swap to the previous stable variant, or a temporary "sticky-version" to keep all traffic on the last known-good model while you investigate.

If you need us to sign an exception for SLA behavior while this is mitigated, we can expedite procurement/approval on our side. We aim to avoid a full rollback unless absolutely necessary.

Appreciate a quick read and recommended immediate action.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Head of Platform Operations
OrthonoVA

Attachment: telemetry snippet referenced (orthonova_trace_20270614.txt)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria@orthonova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:12:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevated latency on Pilot canary - request for auto-fallback/pinning

Hi Maria — thanks for the data and heads-up.

Short answer: yes, we can enable both options; I recommend the following immediate steps to reduce user impact while preserving telemetry for root cause:

1) Enable "auto-swap" fallback for the pilot route with a conservative health window (3x baseline p95 over a 5-minute rolling window) so we immediately fail traffic to the last stable variant.
2) If auto-swap is undesired, enable a temporary sticky-version (pin) to lock the route to the previous stable model for an initial 2-hour window while we triage.
3) Capture a paired telemetry snapshot before/after change (I'll request Rishi to attach the runbook & snapshot).

Operational asks for your team:
- Confirm whether you prefer auto-swap or sticky-version for the first action (auto-swap will restore latency faster; sticky-version preserves current routing but may retain impacted requests depending on cache/kv distribution).
- If sticky-version is chosen, please sign the SLA exception authorization below (one-liner reply is fine).

If you approve, I'll also loop in Laura (product lead) to sign off on a temporary SLA carveout for the pilot and Aditya to confirm any commercial implications.

Proposed immediate action: enable auto-swap && snapshot telemetry. Please reply "auto-swap approved" or "pin approved".

—Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Thanks for the context. I approve a temporary SLA carveout to allow an automated model-swap (auto-swap) for the OrthonoVA pilot under these constraints:

- Approval window: up to 4 hours from the moment auto-swap is triggered.
- Required artifacts before action: sticky-version-runbook-v1.pdf, paired telemetry snapshot (pre/post), and an in-call owner from Redwood SRE (Rishi).
- Post-action: Redwood to file a change note in the deal record (Deal RDW-ORT-42) and notify OrthonoVA of outcome and next steps within 1 hour.

Kimberly — please proceed with auto-swap if telemetry meets the threshold and Rishi confirms the snapshot. Aditya, please update the HubSpot deal and note the SLA carveout under 'Pilot exceptions'.

Laura Bennett

Following up with the technical runbook and artifacts. I'm on-call and will own the execution window if you want me to flip auto-swap.

Attachments (stubs):
- sticky-version-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook: steps to enable sticky-version, auto-swap thresholds, emergency rollback)
- orthonova_canary_telemetry_snapshot.json (pre-action snapshot)
- change_request_RDW-ORT-42.docx (signed carveout form template)

Runbook highlights (short):
- Validate paired telemetry: check p50/p95/p99 and request error-rate delta > 0.5% over baseline.
- Set auto-swap threshold: rolling 5m p95 > 3x baseline OR sustained p50 > 250ms for 2 consecutive windows.
- Execute auto-swap: route-level swap to previous variant; confirm KV cache warm-up for 5m.
- If auto-swap fails to stabilize in 10m, escalate to full rollback and notify orthonova@secure.
- Post-action telemetry: collect a 30-minute rolling snapshot, upload to shared Drive, and file change note in HubSpot.

I will attach the runbook and snapshot to this thread. If OrthonoVA confirms "auto-swap approved" I will begin the action and post updates every 5 minutes.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
